Market stance

Friday's rout broke SPY's $760 swing low, took QQQ below its 30-week trend, and split the group between dip-buyers (Enrich, DiCarlo) and capital-protectors (iain, Venu, Prof) heading into the weekend.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • Friday rout — SPY −1.77% on 2.06x volume, QQQ −3.47% on 2.32x (Prof: Nasdaq fell 4% in one session, his figure); SMH −6.98% as semis led down
  • VIX and forced selling — Prof: $VIX down 20% off the highs; 5 leveraged funds reportedly facing liquidation (his report, unverified) — plus his warning not to carry shorts into the weekend
  • VRT earnings beat — Enrich's figures: revenue $4.3B vs $3.8B expected, EPS $2.21 vs $1.82, free cash flow $652M vs $373M, orders growing roughly twice as fast as sales
  • 200-day test — Venu: the major indexes approaching their 200-day average is where a shakeout and a breakdown part ways — the live question for next week
  • Midterms days away — Prof: watching portfolios get destroyed just days before the midterms; iain: protect capital first, and a bounce is not a bottom

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A risk-off Friday, and the group's split is now the story. DiCarlo supplied the levels: SPY's $760 daily swing low breached with a reclaim-by-next-week deadline, SPCX's daily swing low broken with a $144 reclaim-or-$120 deadline over the next two sessions, ON back at discount for an 8–12 month long, and NOW back in the buy zone. Enrich supplied the buying: VRT on a quoted earnings beat, RKLB as debatably his highest-conviction setup with active buying at long-term support after the neutron delay, and two wait-for-it zones — BE $160–$170 as a generational gift and NBIS $130 as a second-mortgage neckline, both roughly 16% below Friday's closes. Prof supplied the weekend warning: VIX down 20% off the highs, a report (unverified) of 5 leveraged funds facing liquidation, and the line that nobody in their right mind holds shorts after Nasdaq fell 4% in one session — do not carry shorts into the weekend. Venu supplied the frame: indexes approaching the 200-day average is the shakeout-versus-breakdown moment, and the selloff has broadened from semis into software. iain supplied the discipline: protect capital first, a 50% drawdown is not a 50% discount, and the bounce two weeks ago was a textbook dead cat bounce. Remz supplied the day-trade tape: SNDK puts $2 to $20, APP puts up 150%+, COIN puts 100%, DELL puts 150%, TSLA calls 300%+ — completed trades, not forward setups — plus shorting pops on tech and a DELL-after-INTC wonder. Sean posted nothing new in this window; his visible posts are the Oct 28–29 system series. Your process sides with the protectors: no clean qualifier fires today — the nearest live levels are SPCX's $144 reclaim (6.89% away, a repair not a long entry), VRT's 50-week reclaim (4.81% away, a falling name's repair), and BE/NBIS zones 16% below Friday's closes; everything else is a hold at the highs (AAPL, MSFT, TSLA), a broken level (SPY $760, QQQ's 30-week trend, SPCX's swing low), or a thesis buy with no stated level (ON, NOW, RKLB's support).

  • Accounts scanned (7): Sean trades @SRxTrades · iain @ohiain · Enrich Trades @enrichtrades · Remz @Remzztrades · Prof @TheProfInvestor · Venu @Venu_7_ · Peter DiCarlo @pdicarlotrader. Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account; posts truncated in the extraction itself (Sean's system post, iain's capital post, Venu's shakeout post, Prof's Trump post) are quoted only to the visible cutoff. Where a post is truncated, the feed says so instead of guessing the rest.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Fri Oct 30, 2026 close — this run is Saturday morning, so Friday's close is the latest completed close. Every distance-to-trigger in this feed uses the regular close. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader's framing, and it's labeled every time. Figure check on QQQ: Prof's “Nasdaq fell 4%” is his session figure; the QQQ regular close is −3.47%. No after-hours price is stated anywhere in this window, so no after-hours line appears in any panel.
  • Sector lines: each card's sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Fri Oct 30, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL→XLK, MSFT/NOW→IGV, NVDA/ON→SMH, GOOGL/META→XLC, AMZN/TSLA→XLY, RKLB→UFO (space — best fit), VRT→XLI (industrials — best fit), BE→ICLN (clean energy — best fit), NBIS→CLOU (cloud computing — best fit), SPCX→IWM (small-cap proxy for a SPAC/new-issue ETF — best fit, noted here). Best-fit choices are noted here, not hidden.
  • Where none of the seven commented on an index, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” IWM and TLT are unavailable this window: no trader mentioned small caps, bonds or rates. SPY and QQQ carry tone labels plus DiCarlo's and Prof's stated levels where given; the panels say which parts are trader levels and which are our chart checks.
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). No clean qualifier fires today: the nearest live levels are SPCX's $144 reclaim (6.89% away, a repair not a long entry), VRT's 50-week reclaim (4.81% away, a falling name's repair), and the BE/NBIS zones roughly 16% below Friday's closes. Constructive holds, not entries: AAPL (at the highs), MSFT, TSLA (above every average). Broken levels: SPY $760, QQQ's 30-week trend, SPCX's daily swing low, NVDA's PDL 212.08 (yesterday's trigger, lost Friday). Thesis buys, no stated level: RKLB (support, no number), ON (discount, no number), NOW (buy zone, no number). Completed trades, not setups: Remz's Friday put wins and TSLA calls.
  • Coverage note: nothing is carried over silently. Yesterday's BTC, COST, INTC and SNDK rows drop because today's posts do not repeat those calls. TSLA and RKLB reappear only under today's calls, which differ from yesterday's (TSLA via Remz's completed day trade, not Enrich's watchlist; RKLB via Enrich's new highest-conviction support buy, not the completed $59 gap fill). NVDA's panel references yesterday's PDL 212.08 only as context for Friday's close — it is not a new trader call.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. No trader posted a retrievable chart image for a covered name in the visible posts this window, so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all 52 computable lines passed within 0.5% (SPCX has no 30-week MA or 50-week EMA: too young, about 20 weekly closes). The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
